 Namma Metro Blue Line Trials Begin on Bengaluru’s East Corridor
 By Ayesha Siddiqui 
 November 19, 2026 
 0 
 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp 
 Namma Metro Blue Line trial runs have begun on an approximately 6-km section between the Baiyappanahalli depot and the Doddanekundi area in east Bengaluru, according to a report by MagicBricks. The testing is not passenger service: engineers are checking track alignment, power supply, signalling and clearances before the corridor can undergo statutory safety inspections.
 The test train was reported to have moved from the Baiyappanahalli depot towards KR Puram and Doddanekundi along the elevated mainline viaduct. The testing follows initial depot and test-track activities, including checks involving the corridor’s third-rail and cable-charging systems, the report said.
 The Blue Line is being developed in two parts. Phase 2A covers the 19.75-km stretch from Central Silk Board to KR Puram, while Phase 2B covers the 38.44-km route from KR Puram to Kempegowda International Airport through Nagawara and Hebbal. Together, the phases are planned as a 58.19-km elevated corridor with about 29 to 30 stations.
 MagicBricks reported that construction across the project had crossed roughly 72%, although substantial civil work remained around Central Silk Board, KR Puram and Hebbal. The report also placed the estimated project cost at Rs 14,788 crore, with approximately Rs 2,762 crore set aside for land acquisition.
 The reported testing milestone does not establish a confirmed opening date. The Central Silk Board–KR Puram section is currently targeting a mid-2027 opening, with some estimates extending to late 2027. The full corridor to Kempegowda International Airport is being indicated for late 2027 or early 2028, subject to construction progress, testing, safety inspections and statutory clearances.
 The corridor is intended to link major employment and interchange areas across Bengaluru. Its route runs through the Outer Ring Road area, KR Puram, Nagawara and Hebbal before reaching the airport. Planned interchange points include Central Silk Board with the Yellow Line, KR Puram with the Purple Line, Nagawara with the Pink Line, and Hebbal or Kempapura with a future Orange Line connection, according to the report.
 The line’s urban importance comes from the areas it is intended to connect rather than from the trial run alone. Central Silk Board, Bellandur, Marathahalli and Kadubeesanahalli form a major employment corridor, while KR Puram and Hebbal are important transfer points between east, north and central Bengaluru. A direct rail connection to the airport would also provide an alternative to road-based journeys along heavily congested corridors.
 The project is being built through areas where construction activity already affects traffic movement. The report noted ongoing work around major junctions and referred to traffic diversions near Ballari Road linked to an adjacent elevated-road project. These overlapping works mean that the short-term experience for residents and road users may remain difficult even as the metro corridor advances.
 Stations on the airport-facing route are designed with wider concourses, larger fare gates and additional space for passengers carrying luggage, the report said. The corridor is also being equipped for modern signalling and driverless-capable trains, although passenger operations will depend on the completion of all required systems and approvals.
 For commuters, the immediate implication is limited: the Blue Line is still unavailable for public travel. The trial runs indicate that testing has moved onto part of the mainline, but they do not by themselves confirm readiness for commercial operations. The next significant milestones will be the completion of remaining civil and systems work, integrated testing, safety assessment and statutory clearance before any passenger opening is announced.
